parts:
Hi All,

It is great to read these forums and see the RApache examples!

I have just installed R / RApache on Ubuntu Hardy and I am trying to
get it all to run properly. However, I am running into a problem:

When looking at RApacheInfo everything looks fine: see:
http://173.203.212.233/R/RApacheInfo

However, I also added the Hello World example (I did rename it to
test.R, but I dont thinks thats causing the problem....)

I added:

<Location /R/test>
ROutputErrors
Options indexes FollowSymLinks
SetHandler r-handler
RFileHandler /var/www/R/test.R
</Location>

to my apache config file, and added:

main <- function() {
setContentType("text/html")
png("/var/www/images/hello.png")
plot(sample(100,100),col=1:8,pch=19)
dev.off()
cat("<html>")
cat("<body>")
cat("<h1>hello world</h1>")
cat('<img src="/images/hello.png"')
cat("</body>")
cat("</html>")
}

to the file test.R in var/www/R/

So I hoped to see a nice graph. However, I get the following when
opening http://173.203.212.233/R/test in a browser:

<div style="background-color:#eee; padding: 20px 20px 20px 20px; font-
size: 14pt; border: 1px solid red;"><code>RApache Warning/Error!!!
<br><br>ParsedFile(/var/www/R/test.R) failed!</code></div>

(its not even parsed as html...)

Now I tried changing the permissions on test.R to make sure the file
is readable and executable for all... That failed. And, besides that I
dont have a clue where to start.

Could anyone give me a hand getting this started? Perhaps someone can
tell me if the RApacheInfo file displays anything it should not
display. Or whether the warning is caused by a known misconfiguration
from my side?

Help would be greatly appreciated.

parts:
Hi Jeff,

Thanks a lot for the quick reply. Apologies for getting back this
late..

I reinstalled my apache server and all since I was kind of stuck. Now,
RApache is running and I can run R scripts a its supposed to be.
However, the helloWorld example still gave me problems. Some issues
and fixes:

ISSUE 1:
I installed R using:
# sudo apt-get install r-base-dev apache2-mpm-prefork apache2-prefork-
dev

After installing RApache and creating the helloWorld.R example I
pointed a browser to the page and got a bunch of warnings. The first
being:
Error in X11(paste("png::", filename, sep = ""), width, height,
pointsize, : unable to start device PNG

This warning seemed due to the version of R where by using:

# sudo nano /etc/apt/sources.list
and adding the appropriate mirror

# gpg --keyserver subkeys.pgp.net --recv-key E2A11821
# gpg -a --export E2A11821 | sudo apt-key add -
# sudo apt-get update

And installing a update. The issue was solved
# sudo apt-get install r-base-dev


ISSUE 2:
This removed the first waring. However, it got me to bump into the
next one:
Error in png("/var/www/images/hello.png") : X11 module cannot be
loaded

This apparently is a know issue when running R to create png's in
batch mode see: http://cran.r-project.org/doc/FAQ/R-FAQ.html#How-do-I-produce-PNG-graphics-in-batch-mode_003f

Then, I tried to move over to GDD. I installed GDD from command line,
but apparently this is installed for this user only. Hence, when
running RApache and calling library(GDD) I get: there is no package
called GGD...

Can anyone tell me how to make the installed libraries accesssible for
RApache?

ISSUE 3:
One thing I bumped into is that ftp-ing the .R files from the server
to my locl computer (Windows) and then putting them back breaks them,
resulting in the:

<div style="background-color:#eee; padding: 20px 20px 20px 20px;
font-
size: 14pt; border: 1px solid red;"><code>RApache Warning/Error!!!
<br><br>ParsedFile(/var/www/R/test.R) failed!</code></div>

I mentioned in the first post. If I find out why I will let you know.

Again, Jeff, thanks for your time. I hope my first fix helps someone,
and once I find out what's wrong with issue 3 I will update it. If
anyone can give me a hand on the second one that would be great!

Cheers,

Maurits

Hmm... I tried to respond and something went wrong so I lost a bunch
of text.

Jeff, Thanks for your response!

I proceeded and ran into a number of probles:

1. I apparently was running an old verison of R - This caused PNG to
be false when looking under capabilities() - in R from command line.
The update solved this problem

Solved using:
sudo nano /etc/apt/sources.list // And updating the Cran mirror

gpg --keyserver subkeys.pgp.net --recv-key E2A11821
gpg -a --export E2A11821 | sudo apt-key add -

sudo apt-get update


2. Next I am running into a problem with X11. Aparently this is a know
problem (see R FAQ on PNG in batch mode) and I decide to use GDD for
images instead.

I openened R in command line
Installed GDD
tried some graphs (all worked and where written to the files)
changed the code in the helloWorld example: see: http://173.203.212.233/R/helloWorld
(to see the R file http://173.203.212.233/R/helloWorld.R

However, GDD is not working. I think it is a multiuser problem. Is
there any way to enable usage of libraries for all users?

3. I also noticed something else: Everytime I tried to edit the .R
file that is actually being run, I stumbled onto the error that made
me open this post:

<div style="background-color:#eee; padding: 20px 20px 20px 20px;
font-
size: 14pt; border: 1px solid red;"><code>RApache Warning/Error!!!
<br><br>ParsedFile(/var/www/R/test.R) failed!</code></div>

This apparently means the .R file is "corrupt". At least, editing on
the server trough (e.g.) nano yields no problem. Only when I get the
file onto my local computer (Windows) and get it back the file "fails
to parse".

Anyone any ideas on how to solve this?

parts:
Hi Jeff,

Thanks again for the support!

I fixed the issues! Check out my great hello world plot at:
http://173.203.212.233/R/helloWorld

Some things that might be of help to people:

1. I had to set the rights for my virtual host to enable apache to
read and write
2. I had to create an empty hello.png file which was readable and
writeable by all..
-- Those, in combination with the bunch of remarks above got the
example to work.

I also figures out what was causing the

<div style="background-color:#eee; padding: 20px 20px 20px 20px;
font-
size: 14pt; border: 1px solid red;"><code>RApache Warning/Error!!!
<br><br>ParsedFile(/var/www/R/test.R) failed!</code></div>

error:

I was trying to edit R files on my windows machine and updating them
to the linux server. This messed up the file encoding (This happened
in R, not in Dreamweaver what I expected.) The quickest fix I could
find is using notepad++ in R and explicitly saving the R files for
Unix.

But, now I am finally set and can start the actual project I wanted to
do using RApache. Thanks everyone here for the great comments in the
different discussions and special thanks to Jeff!

I will let you know once my project is up and running and share it
with the group.

Cheers,

Maurits
